issues.legal_issue: Consistent and specifically corroborated testimony against particular accused may support their convictions even when other accused are acquitted on the same evidence.
material_facts: The witnesses were interested because of bitter enmity between the two groups, so their testimony was scrutinised with greater care.
The witnesses consistently attributed specific acts to the convicted accused, and those acts were corroborated by the medical evidence and circumstances.
The other accused were acquitted because specific acts were absent or inconsistently attributed to them.
issues.conclusion: The acquittal of the other accused did not prevent the court from relying on the same witnesses' consistent, specific and corroborated evidence to uphold these convictions.
issues.legal_principle: Interested witnesses' evidence is not to be rejected solely because of their interest, but must be scrutinised with greater care. Specific acts consistently attributed to an accused and corroborated by medical evidence and the circumstances can safely support conviction. No earlier cases or particular statutory provisions were relied on for this evidentiary principle.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_after_partial_acquittal and witnesses_interested and specific_acts_consistently_attributed and evidence_corroborated

predicates.criminal_appeal_after_partial_acquittal: The proceeding is a criminal appeal against convictions in a case where some other accused were acquitted.
predicates.witnesses_interested: The witnesses had a relationship or other interest that called for their testimony to be scrutinised with greater care.
predicates.specific_acts_consistently_attributed: The witnesses consistently attributed specific acts to the accused whose convictions are challenged.
predicates.evidence_corroborated: The attributed acts were corroborated by medical evidence and the circumstances of the case.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows partial acquittals, interested witnesses' testimony supports conviction if they consistently attribute specific acts to the accused and that evidence is corroborated.

issues.legal_issue: Constructive liability may be based on the proved circumstances and the transaction as a whole when accused persons participate in a collective armed attack.
material_facts: The accused were members of an unlawful assembly armed with spears and chased and surrounded the deceased.
The convicted accused were consistently said to have inflicted injuries during the attack, and the deceased then escaped into a nearby house where the attackers followed him.
The witness who was inside the house turned hostile, leaving no accepted direct account of what happened there.
The deceased had numerous injuries, and the medical evidence established that an injury and the cumulative effect of the injuries were fatal.
issues.conclusion: The proved circumstances were sufficient to invoke Section 34 or Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code against the accused, considering the transaction as a whole.
issues.legal_principle: For constructive liability under Section 34 or Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, the court considers the relevant ingredients and proved circumstances, including the formation of an unlawful assembly, the weapons carried and the accused's active roles. The circumstances of the transaction as a whole may support liability even where direct evidence of the final stage of the attack is unavailable. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenging_constructive_liability and unlawful_assembly_formed and accused_armed_and_active and coordinated_attack_continued and attack_caused_fatal_injuries

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_constructive: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging liability imposed for the acts of a group.
predicates.unlawful_assembly_formed: The accused formed part of an unlawful assembly during the incident.
predicates.accused_armed_and_active: The accused were armed and actively participated in the attack.
predicates.coordinated_attack_continued: The group pursued the victim and continued the attack as part of the same transaction.
predicates.attack_caused_fatal_injuries: The attack caused injuries that were fatal, individually or cumulatively.

issues.definition: Constructive liability is upheld in an appeal when an unlawful assembly's armed members actively pursue and attack a victim in a coordinated transaction that causes fatal injuries.

issues.legal_issue: A delay in reporting does not undermine the prosecution case when it is not inordinate and is consistent with efforts to obtain prompt assistance for an injured person.
material_facts: The deceased was alive after the attack, and those present first arranged to take him to the police station or hospital.
The deceased died on the way, and the report was made later that same night, about five hours after the incident.
issues.conclusion: The reporting delay was not inordinate and did not require the prosecution case to be viewed with suspicion.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the delay in light of the circumstances, including the effort to take the injured person for assistance and the fact that the report was made that same night. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction and report_made_same_night and delay_not_inordinate and efforts_made_to_get_assistance

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.report_made_same_night: The report was made on the night of the incident.
predicates.delay_not_inordinate: The time taken before the report was made was not inordinate in the circumstances.
predicates.efforts_made_to_get_assistance: Those present were occupied with efforts to obtain assistance for the injured person.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, a same-night report made after a non-inordinate delay does not undermine the prosecution when those present were seeking assistance for the injured person.
